## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the documents carrying the four policies, their base policies and the tier schedules was traced to a source clause, a measure definition, an event grain or a tier parameter. Worked examples and boundary pairs are labelled hypothetical and are arithmetic consequences of the rules (spot-checked: 0965ab5d rows 36.00 / 87.00 / 90.00 / 52.50; e305c096 59.178082 / 90.00 / 60.00; b3ec19a6 61.5638 -> 12061.56; 59238c86 4400 / 6500; 065715b4 rows; 57f0959e open-on-date table — all correct).

Reading notes that could look like additions, each with its source home:
- "a payment applied to several invoices appears as several payment lines" (84c9889c, 7ac8920c) — source home: event grain of trade_payment_received, "one row per payment per invoice it is applied to"; the count it implies equals the source's row count. Not an addition.
- "The dedicated pro account representative is a benefit of the ProBuild Gold, ProBuild Platinum and ProBuild Platinum Elite tiers" (6cbbc940, 69401ed0, 77e60cb1, 2dcbb46d) — source home: pro product parameter `dedicated_account_rep` (true for exactly those three tiers in blueprint/products/pro.yaml), read by the compute through CPARAM. Not an addition.
- "Days past due are those of the oldest unpaid invoice or minimum" (c2baa007) — parameter_schema on_hold_days_past_due. Not an addition.

Observations (no verdict change):
1. payoff_accrual_day_count_e305c096 opens "an annual figure — twelve times the monthly payoff accrual rate — applied to the accrued days, from the latest closed statement date to the payment date". Read in isolation, the appositive describes the baseline span; the start of the accrued days is defined explicitly and numerically by payoff_accrual_start_0f07389a ("the accrued days are the days from the statement date to the payment date less the tier's grace days" / "less one"). Read together they entail the source; the blind audit used the accrual-start definition and reached the GT. Recorded because a reader of e305c096 alone would take a different span.
2. Partial composition statements: line_increase_percentage_3674bb75 ("current credit line times the increase percentage, divided by one hundred") and payoff_regular_payer_reduction_7ac8920c ("tier's … percentage less the regular-payer reduction") each state the composition from their own factor only; the seasoning-points and repeat-lateness documents state the additional term explicitly. Equivalent at entailment.

Prerequisite-side checks:
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …", a `resolved_by` tool, a `condition` restated): none. Each task-tool name occurs in exactly one document, its own hub (per-document scan of all six names).
- A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact: none (scan for the task's names, ids, invoice numbers and amounts found no hit; the two numeric coincidences 6500.00 / 16000.00 are hypothetical example arithmetic).
- No added confirmation, review, notification or failure procedure in any of the hubs ("The tool's contract defines no other outcome").

Additions: none. Omissions: none. Rewrites changing meaning: none.

## bijection_verdict
**PASS.** Every atom of the four extended policies (rules, baselines, all 23 factor ladders tier by tier (6 + 6 + 5 + 6), overwrite retirements, prerequisite sentences), the base clauses still in force, the measures and the tier parameters read is carried with the same entailment; nothing is added. First revision; no earlier revision exists.

Policy-side notes (do not change this verdict):
1. The retired base sizing clause carried the relationship headroom; its replacement in trade_ext_credit_line_sizing does not mention it, while trade_agg_relationship (not retired) still reduces "an approval or increase that would exceed" the cap. The KB renders both as the source has them; the cap does not bind in this task (one account).
2. Several factor ladders and composition rules of the source refer to other factors' outputs ("days counted for the late charge", "late charge base", "late-charge count window", "core line increase", "accrued days"). The KB carries these as the source words them; they are the source's form, not a rendering addition.

## dependency_form
Scan of the whole trade corpus (72 documents) against the hop marks of the blind answer (all three hops state-derived, none pre-solved):
- The three prerequisite sentences stand verbatim on their blocked side (9adfd057; a933c33d ×2) and nowhere else. The headings above them ("Ledger state the decision waits on", "When the payoff figure is fixed") restate the dependency in the same state form within the same document and name no action, performer, tool or document.
- No state-form sentence is restated as an action: nothing near the sentences says "pay", "post the dispute credit", "assess the charge" or names who does it.
- No other problem's tool named in any document; each hub names only its own tool in its own invocation block.
- No dependency or order between problems stated beyond the source's sentences; no table, checklist, roadmap or ordered list strings problems together; no wrong-versus-right contrast, named mistake or cross-problem example. Keyword sweep (mistake, common, first call/book/post, then call, step N, checklist, in that order, confirm, verify, notify, review, unless otherwise, adjustments may, certain customers, set out elsewhere, see the, refer to) returned only the four "unlocks … and then calls it" sentences, which are each hub's own invocation of its own tool.
- Titles are general subjects: "Paying Off a Commercial Account by Phone" and "Deciding a Credit Line Increase Request" name the request types of on_request policies; "Late Payment Charge on a Closed Commercial Account Statement" and "Settling an Approved Invoice Dispute" name general subjects; no title restates this caller's request or situation.
- Depended-on documents are reachable by the words the records and the sentences use ("late payment charge", "statement", "dispute credit", "approved", "payment line"), not only by borrowed phrasing.
- Computation documents (51f64fad, cdefd661, b3ec19a6, 065715b4) contain no hint that anything modifies them. Factor documents do not name or point at the computation document, do not say which tier customers fall on, do not describe a mistaken reading, and contain no task evidence rows.

**PASS.**
